I’ve built dashboards, contributed to digital systems and explored how stories and audience psychology shape engagement. I’m applying to the Tamatem Internship Program in Amman, and I want to turn that experience into useful work for Tamatem.

Ideas for Tamatem

Three proposed concepts. I have not built any of them yet, and each could start small.

Arabic Gamer Personality Map

Proposed concept

What makes different players return to a game? I would explore public player feedback and audience research to identify recurring motivations, then organize the findings into a simple dashboard. The goal is to generate useful questions and campaign hypotheses, not to assume every player behaves the same way.

Initial version can be researched using public information and built with Excel/Python.

Culture Collision Lab

Proposed concept

One campaign idea, several local interpretations. I would create sample creative directions for selected Arabic-speaking markets, research local context and gather structured feedback on relevance, clarity and tone.

Initial version can be researched using public information and built with Excel/Python.

Comment-to-Update Pipeline

Proposed concept

Player comments can contain useful signals. I would build a lightweight tagging system to group public feedback into recurring themes such as feature requests, confusion, technical issues and positive experiences, then summarize patterns for team review.

Initial version can be researched using public information and built with Excel/Python.

How I think

One small example of my approach. It is a proposed method, not a finished study.

  1. Observation

    The same game can appeal to people for different reasons.

  2. Question

    Which motivations appear in public player feedback?

  3. Method

    Review a sample, tag themes, summarize patterns.

  4. Output

    A simple insight sheet and campaign hypotheses.

Public comments are directional signals, not a representative sample of all players.

How I would approach the work

Start small, use public or approved data, document assumptions, and agree on a useful question with the team. Build a simple first version, gather feedback and improve it. Where appropriate, define a measure of success before testing, such as response rate, engagement, recurring feedback themes or task completion.

Potential contributions

Areas I am curious about and keen to learn in. These are interests, not claims of professional expertise.

Player Intelligence & Research

  • Explore player motivations, feedback patterns and engagement opportunities through structured research and data analysis.
  • Turn scattered information into organized insights and actionable recommendations.

Creative Marketing & Localization

  • Develop culturally relevant campaign concepts tailored to different Arabic-speaking audiences.
  • Explore creative testing through audience psychology, storytelling and visual content.

Digital Process & Product Improvement

  • Identify friction points in user journeys and propose practical improvements.
  • Build simple dashboards and tracking systems to support better team decisions.

Why Tamatem

Fashion Queen was one of my games. It was also the first game aimed at women players in Arabic, and Tamatem brought it here.

That is what I admire: you give young people the space and the tools to grow and be creative. I want to learn how that works from the inside.

How I work

Team first. One of my greatest strengths is my ability to communicate effectively, build strong relationships, and support others in finding solutions to challenges.

I negotiate well. I listen, stay calm and bring people toward an idea I believe in.

Ideas under pressure. When a problem gets deep, a solution tends to click, and I follow it through.

Dual studies in one minute

My degree alternates three months at the university with three months inside a company, over four years: eight training periods, and I’ve done three. Al-Quds launched it in 2015 on the German model, calls it the first of its kind in the Arab world, and works with more than 200 partner companies in Palestine.

A company gets a trainee who comes back for several periods and learns the business from inside.
